title: Finding your way around the menus
target: Where Supermarket Simulator keeps its own menus, its settings and its key bindings, so a change is made in the right place rather than hunted for.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop open or a save loaded

steps.do: Expect pausing to open a menu of its own rather than a list of buttons.
steps.because: pausing opens an escape menu of its own (EscapeMenuManager)

steps.do: Know that tabs and sub-tabs are separate layers.
steps.because: the menu's tabs are run by a manager of their own and sub-tabs have another (TabManager, SubTabManager)

steps.do: Be deliberate about leaving, because quitting is sorted into kinds.
steps.because: quitting is sorted into kinds and transitions between screens are typed as well (QuitType, TransitionType)

steps.do: Go to settings for a change rather than to the menu you happen to be in.
steps.because: the game keeps a settings manager, a container for settings and the data behind them (SettingsManager, SettingsContainer, SettingsData)

steps.do: Look for the category a setting belongs to instead of scrolling everything.
steps.because: the settings menu is managed and grouped by category (SettingsMenuManager, SettingCategoryCanvas)

steps.do: Treat each option as its own entry.
steps.because: an individual setting is an entry of its own (SettingEntry)

steps.do: Rebind keys in the interface built for it rather than editing anything by hand.
steps.because: keys can be rebound through a manager, a loader and a settings object, and the interface is built from an entry view, a tab view and a bridge (KeybindManager, KeybindLoader, KeybindSettings, KeybindEntryView, KeybindingTabView, KeybindingUIBridge)

steps.do: Know the pause mark is the game's own art rather than something this site drew.
steps.because: the game ships its own pause icon for the menus (asset name: Icon_PictoIcon_Pause)

commonMistakes: Looking for a setting inside the tab you were using rather than in the settings menu.
Rebinding a key in a controller screen when the binding lives in its own interface.
Leaving by the wrong kind of quit when a save was wanted.
Assuming a sub-tab is the same thing as a tab.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
